sections.body: This topic would synthesize cases where an optimization is beneficial only under particular inputs, paths, hardware resources, or program contexts.
sections.heading: Section 1

sections.body: Aestimo's bzip2 case shows training input materially changes inlining performance, with combined training, xml training, and best-case per-input FDO producing different gains. Machine-learning compilation frames the same issue through context-dependent choices such as thread coarsening. WCC and distributed quantum compilation add timing and resource-sensitive examples, where optimizing the wrong path or consuming limited communication resources can blunt or reverse expected benefits.
sections.heading: Section 2

sections.body: The topic should emphasize conditionality rather than a universal ranking of optimizations, since the evidence spans conventional programs, WCET-oriented embedded compilation, and distributed quantum compilation.
